questions.question: A trader borrows N800,000 and repays it with 3 equal payments at the end of each year. Interest is 15% per annum effective. Find each payment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The equation of value is 800,000 = X(v + v^2 + v^3) = X a_3|, with a_3| = 2.2832 at 15%, so X = N350,382. Option C accumulates the loan for 3 years and divides by 3, which overcharges because the earlier payments reduce the debt sooner. Option D uses simple interest on the full loan, and option A ignores interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A debt of N300,000 due at time 2 years is to be settled instead by two equal payments X, one at time 1 year and one at time 4 years. Using compound interest at 10% per annum effective, find X to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Equating present values: X(v + v^4) = 300,000v^2, so X = 247,933.88/(0.909091 + 0.683013) = N155,727. Option A ignores interest, option D halves the present value of the debt without discounting the payments, and option C places the second payment at time 3 instead of time 4.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The present value at time 0 of a series of future payments is N250,000, using compound interest at 8% per annum effective. What is the value of the same series at time 3 years, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Under compound interest the value of a whole stream at time t equals its PV times (1 + i)^t, so 250,000(1.08)^3 = N314,928. Option D discounts instead of accumulating, option C uses simple interest, and option B accumulates for only 2 years.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The accumulated value at time 4 years of a series of deposits is N500,000, at 10% per annum effective compound interest. What is the value of the same series at time 0, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: PV = AV x v^4 = 500,000(1.1)^-4 = N341,507. Option A uses simple interest (dividing by 1.4), option B multiplies by (0.9)^4, which uses 1 - i instead of v = 1/(1 + i), and option C accumulates further instead of discounting.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A machine costs N500,000 now and produces N200,000 at the end of each year. Using a discount rate of 10% per annum effective, in which year does the cumulative discounted cash flow first become positive (the discounted payback period)?
questions.explanation: Cumulative discounted cash flows are -N318,182, -N152,893, -N2,630, N133,973 at the ends of years 1 to 4, so the project first breaks even in year 4. Option D is the ordinary (undiscounted) payback, since 2.5 years of N200,000 recovers N500,000. Option C is wrong because the discounted total after 3 years is still just below N500,000.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Payments of N40,000 at time 0.5 years and N60,000 at time 1.5 years are valued at an effective rate of compound interest of 10% per annum. What is their present value, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: With compound interest the discount factor for t years is (1.1)^-t even for fractional t: 40,000(1.1)^-0.5 + 60,000(1.1)^-1.5 = N90,146. Option B uses simple interest for the part-years, option D rounds the times up to whole years, and option C treats 10% as a nominal half-yearly rate (5% per half-year).

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A contract pays N10,000 at the end of year 1, N20,000 at the end of year 2 and N30,000 at the end of year 3. At 5% per annum effective compound interest, what is the present value, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: PV = 10,000(1.05)^-1 + 20,000(1.05)^-2 + 30,000(1.05)^-3 = N53,580. Option B reverses the order of the payments, which gives a higher value because the big payment would come first. Option D discounts the total from the middle year, and option C is the accumulated value at time 3.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Deposits of N10,000, N20,000 and N30,000 are made at the ends of years 1, 2 and 3 respectively into an account paying 5% per annum effective. What is the balance immediately after the year-3 deposit, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: AV at time 3 = 10,000(1.05)^2 + 20,000(1.05) + 30,000 = N62,025. Option A also gives the last deposit a year of interest, even though it has just been made. Option D reverses the order of the deposits, and option B accumulates all N60,000 for 3 years.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A clinic buys equipment priced at N2,000,000. It pays N500,000 now, N800,000 at the end of year 1 and a final amount X at the end of year 2. The supplier charges 12% per annum effective compound interest. Find X to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: From the equation of value 2,000,000 = 500,000 + 800,000v + Xv^2, X = (1,500,000 - 714,285.71)(1.12)^2 = N985,600. Option C ignores interest, option B is the outstanding amount at time 0 without accumulating it to year 2, and option D forgets to give the year-1 payment one year of interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: How much must be deposited now so that, together with a further deposit of N50,000 at the end of year 2, the account holds N200,000 at the end of year 4? Interest is 7% per annum effective compound.
questions.explanation: At time 4: X(1.07)^4 + 50,000(1.07)^2 = 200,000, so X = (200,000 - 57,245)(1.07)^-4 = N108,907. Option D ignores the interest on the year-2 deposit, option C subtracts the N50,000 without discounting it to time 0, and option B discounts with simple interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: N80,000 is deposited now and another N80,000 one year later, at 9% per annum effective compound interest. After how many years from now (time t, to 2 decimal places) will the fund first reach N200,000?
questions.explanation: For t of at least 1, the equation is 80,000(1.09)^t + 80,000(1.09)^(t-1) = 200,000, so (1.09)^t = 200,000/(80,000 + 73,394.50) and t = 3.08 years. Option A assumes both deposits are made now, option B measures the time from the second deposit instead of from now, and option D divides by 0.09 instead of ln(1.09).

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Using SIMPLE interest at 10% per annum (so N1 at time 0 grows to 1 + 0.1t at time t), find the present value at time 0 of N11,000 due at time 1 year and N12,000 due at time 2 years, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Under simple interest each payment is divided by (1 + it): 11,000/1.1 + 12,000/1.2 = 10,000 + 10,000 = N20,000. Option D switches to compound discounting for the second payment, option C discounts the total for 2 years, and option B ignores discounting.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A rental contract pays N100,000 at the end of year 1, and each later annual payment is 5% more than the one before, with 3 payments in all (at the ends of years 1, 2 and 3). At 10% per annum effective compound interest, what is the present value, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: The payments are 100,000, 105,000 and 110,250, so PV = 100,000(1.1)^-1 + 105,000(1.1)^-2 + 110,250(1.1)^-3 = N260,518. Option B ignores the 5% growth, option A grows the payments at 10% instead of 5% (the PV then equals 3 x 100,000/1.1), and option C discounts at the growth rate instead of the interest rate.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A seller of land in Abuja is offered either N1,000,000 now or N620,000 at the end of each of the next 2 years. At 14% per annum effective compound interest, which offer is better and what is the present value of the instalment offer?

options.a: Lump sum; PV of instalments about N954,140
options.c: Lump sum; PV of instalments about N543,860

questions.explanation: PV of the instalments = 620,000(1.14)^-1 + 620,000(1.14)^-2 = N1,020,930, which exceeds N1,000,000, so the instalments are better. Option A discounts the whole N1,240,000 for 2 years, option D ignores discounting, and option C counts only the first instalment.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: N25,000 is paid at the end of every half-year for 2 years (4 payments). Interest is at a nominal rate of 10% per annum convertible half-yearly. What is the present value of the payments, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Work per half-year at 5%: PV = 25,000[(1.05)^-1 + (1.05)^-2 + (1.05)^-3 + (1.05)^-4] = 25,000 x a_4| at 5% = N88,649. Option B uses 10% per half-year, option D counts only 2 payments at 10%, and option C is the accumulated value after 2 years.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: N30,000 is payable at the end of years 3, 4 and 5 only. At 8% per annum effective compound interest, what is the present value at time 0, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: PV = 30,000(v^3 + v^4 + v^5) at 8% = N66,283; equivalently 30,000 x a_3| x v^2. Option D values payments at years 1 to 3, forgetting the delay, option C delays them one year too many, and option B discounts the total for 3 years.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A project costs N500,000 now and returns N200,000, N250,000 and N150,000 at the ends of years 1, 2 and 3. Its NPV is N1,127 at 10% and -N15,363 at 12% (both effective per annum). Which statement about its internal rate of return is correct?
questions.explanation: NPV falls as the rate rises; it is positive at 10% and negative at 12%, so the rate giving NPV = 0 must lie between them (about 10.13%). Option D is wrong because NPV is still positive at 10%, option C is wrong because NPV is already negative at 12%, and option A assumes the IRR is exactly the midpoint, which is not guaranteed.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A trader deposits N30,000 now and N40,000 in 6 months' time. Interest is at a nominal rate of 12% per annum convertible monthly. What is the balance at the end of 12 months from now, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: The monthly rate is 1%, so the balance is 30,000(1.01)^12 + 40,000(1.01)^6 = N76,266. Option B uses simple interest, option C treats 12% as an effective annual rate, and option D gives the second deposit a full 12 months of interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A microfinance bank charges 18% per annum effective compound interest. A borrower can repay N150,000, N200,000 and N250,000 at the ends of years 1, 2 and 3. What is the largest loan the bank should grant today, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: The loan must equal the present value of the repayments: 150,000(1.18)^-1 + 200,000(1.18)^-2 + 250,000(1.18)^-3 = N422,913. Option B ignores interest, option D treats the repayments as made at the start of each year, and option A discounts the total for 3 years.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A franchise pays N5,000 at the end of year 1, N8,000 at the end of year 2, nothing in year 3, N12,000 at the end of year 4 and N15,000 at the end of year 5. At 7% per annum effective compound interest, find the present value to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: PV = 5,000v + 8,000v^2 + 12,000v^4 + 15,000v^5 at 7% = N31,510. Option D closes the gap and treats the last two payments as due at years 3 and 4, option A is the accumulated value at year 5, and option C discounts the total from year 3.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: An esusu-style savings scheme credits N70,000 at time 1, N50,000 at time 2, N60,000 at time 4 and N90,000 at time 5 (in years). At 9% per annum effective compound interest, what is the accumulated value at time 5, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: AV at time 5 = 70,000(1.09)^4 + 50,000(1.09)^3 + 60,000(1.09) + 90,000 = N318,962. Option A is the value one year later at time 6, option D is the value at time 0, and option C uses a rough simple-interest average.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A loan of N200,000 made now is repaid by X at the end of year 2 and 2X at the end of year 4. At 5% per annum effective compound interest, find X to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Equation of value at time 0: X(1.05)^-2 + 2X(1.05)^-4 = 200,000, so X = 200,000/(0.907029 + 1.645405) = N78,357. Option C ignores interest, option D forgets that the second payment is double, and option A doubles the wrong payment.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: At 6% per annum effective compound interest, Stream P pays N100,000 at times 1 and 4 years and Stream Q pays N95,000 at time 2 and N100,000 at time 3. The present values are N173,549 for P and N168,512 for Q. What is the difference between their values at time 5 (value of P minus value of Q), to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Under compound interest every payment's value at time 5 is its PV times (1.06)^5, so the difference is (N173,549 - N168,512)(1.06)^5 = N6,741; the ranking never changes with the valuation date. Option B is the difference at time 0, option A discounts instead of accumulating, and option C uses simple interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Deposits of N100,000 are made at time 0 and at time 1 year, and the balance at time 2 years is exactly N215,250. Which effective annual rate of compound interest was earned?
questions.explanation: At 5%, 100,000(1.05)^2 + 100,000(1.05) = 110,250 + 105,000 = 215,250, which matches the balance. Option C divides the N15,250 interest by the N200,000 deposited and spreads it over 1 year, ignoring that the deposits are invested for different lengths of time, and the other rates do not satisfy the equation of value.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: N100,000 is deposited at time 0 and N100,000 at time 1 year. By how much is the balance at time 3 years HIGHER at 10% per annum effective than at 5% per annum effective, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: At 5% the balance is 100,000[(1.05)^3 + (1.05)^2] = N226,012; at 10% it is 100,000[(1.1)^3 + (1.1)^2] = N254,100; the difference is N28,088. A higher rate raises accumulated values, unlike present values. Option B compares only the first deposit, option D is simple interest of 5% on the total for 3 years, and option C is the fall in present value, which is a different quantity.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Using an effective rate of DISCOUNT of d = 8% per annum (so that v = 1 - d), find the present value of N50,000 due at the end of year 1 and N50,000 due at the end of year 2, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: With v = 1 - d = 0.92, PV = 50,000(0.92) + 50,000(0.92)^2 = 46,000 + 42,320 = N88,320. Option A treats 8% as a rate of interest, which gives a higher value because v = 1/1.08 = 0.9259. Option B discounts the total for 2 years, and option D mixes compound and simple discounting.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The single value at time 0 obtained by discounting every payment in a series to time 0 at a given rate of interest and adding the results is called the

options.a: accumulated value of the payment stream
options.b: nominal value of the payment stream
options.c: internal rate of return of the payments
options.d: present value of the payment stream

questions.explanation: Discounting each payment back to time 0 with v^t and summing gives the present value of the stream. Option A, the accumulated value, is found by rolling every payment forward to a later date. Option C is a rate of interest, not an amount of money.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The accumulated value of a series of payments at time n means

options.a: the total of all payments discounted back to time 0
options.b: the total of all payments rolled forward with interest to time n
options.c: the interest earned on the last payment only
options.d: the simple sum of the payments with no interest added

questions.explanation: The accumulated (future) value at time n is found by multiplying each payment by (1 + i)^(n - t) and adding, so every payment carries the interest it earns up to time n. Option A describes the present value, and option D ignores the time value of money completely.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: An equation stating that, at a chosen date, the total value of the money paid out equals the total value of the money received, using a given rate of interest, is called
questions.explanation: An equation of value balances the values of incoming and outgoing payments at a common date; it is used to find an unknown payment, time or rate. A discount factor (option A) is just the value v^t of one naira due at time t, and option B relates nominal and effective rates rather than two sets of payments.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Under compound interest, an equation of value is set up for two payment streams at time 0 and again at time 5 years. Which statement is correct?

options.a: The answers differ unless the rate is zero
options.b: Both give the same answer, because every term is multiplied by (1+i)^5
options.c: Only the time-0 version is valid
options.d: Only a date when a payment falls due can be used

questions.explanation: Moving from time 0 to time 5 multiplies every term on both sides by the same factor (1 + i)^5, so the balance and any unknown solved from it are unchanged; any comparison date works under compound interest. Options C and D wrongly restrict the comparison date, and option A would only be a concern under simple interest.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The discount rate at which the net present value of a project's cash flows equals zero is called the
questions.explanation: The internal rate of return is the rate that makes the present value of inflows exactly equal to the present value of outflows. The hurdle rate (option A) is the minimum return a project must reach to be accepted, and the force of interest (option C) is a measure of instantaneous growth.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: For a project with cash flows C_t at times t = 0, 1, ..., n (outflows negative), the expression C_0 + C_1 v + C_2 v^2 + ... + C_n v^n measures the

options.a: accumulated value of the inflows only
options.d: net present value of the project

questions.explanation: Multiplying each net cash flow by v^t and adding gives the net present value, which is the PV of inflows minus the PV of outflows. Option A would need factors (1 + i)^(n - t) and only positive flows, and option B is a length of time, not a sum of discounted amounts.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: For a stream of positive payments due at future dates, with a positive effective rate of compound interest, which statement is NOT true?

options.a: The present value falls when the rate of interest rises
options.b: The present value is less than the simple total of the payments
options.c: The present value equals the accumulated value at the last payment date
options.d: A naira due later adds less to the present value than a naira due sooner

questions.explanation: With i > 0 the accumulated value at the last date is the PV multiplied by (1 + i)^n, which is larger than the PV, so the two are not equal. The other statements are true: discounting makes the PV smaller than the plain total (option B), a higher rate shrinks every v^t (option A), and v^t gets smaller as t grows (option D).

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: If the effective rate of interest used to value a fixed stream of future receipts rises, what happens to the stream's present value?

options.a: It rises, because more interest is earned
options.b: It falls only for payments due within one year
options.c: It is unchanged, since the payments are fixed
options.d: It falls, because each discount factor v^t becomes smaller

questions.explanation: Every discount factor v^t = (1 + i)^-t shrinks as i rises, so the present value of a fixed stream falls. Option A confuses present value with accumulated value, which rises with the rate, and option B is wrong because later payments are affected even more strongly.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: Two streams have the same present value at 8%. Stream X pays mostly in years 1-2; Stream Y pays mostly in years 8-10. If both are revalued at 12% per annum effective, which is true?

options.a: Stream Y now has the lower present value
options.b: Both still have equal present values
options.c: Stream X now has the lower present value

questions.explanation: A higher rate cuts the value of distant payments much more than near ones, because v^t is raised to a larger power. So the later-paying Stream Y loses more and ends up with the lower present value. Option B ignores timing, and option D is wrong because a higher rate lowers present values.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: A debtor and creditor in Kano agree to replace two debts due at different dates with one payment at a new date, with both sides being equally well off at 10% interest. The calculation they need is

options.b: the sum of the two debts with no interest
options.c: a simple average of the two due dates
options.d: an equation of value at a chosen comparison date

questions.explanation: Replacing payments fairly means the new payment must have the same value as the old debts at a common date, which is exactly an equation of value. An average of dates (option C) is only an approximation, and adding the debts with no interest (option B) ignores the time value of money.

questions.topic: Present and Accumulated Values of Payment Streams
questions.question: The number of years needed to recover an initial outlay from a project's cash flows after each cash flow has been discounted for the time value of money is called the
questions.explanation: The discounted payback period counts how long it takes for cumulative discounted cash flows to cover the initial cost. The internal rate of return (option A) is a rate, not a length of time, and the hurdle rate (option B) is the minimum acceptable return.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At an effective rate of interest i = 3% per annum, what is the value of a_12| (the present value of an annuity-immediate of 1 per year for 12 years)? (3 decimal places.)
questions.explanation: a_12| = (1 - v^12)/i = (1 - 1.03^-12)/0.03 = 9.954. Option C (14.192) is s_12|, the accumulated value at the end of the term rather than the present value, and B and D do not match the formula.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At an effective rate of interest i = 3% per annum, what is the value of s_12| (the accumulated value of an annuity-immediate of 1 per year for 12 years)? (3 decimal places.)
questions.explanation: s_12| = ((1 + i)^12 - 1)/i = (1.03^12 - 1)/0.03 = 14.192. Option A (9.954) is a_12|, the present value at the start, and it must be smaller than s_12| because it is not accumulated with interest; C and D do not fit the formula.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The international actuarial symbol for the present value of an ordinary annuity (annuity-immediate, payments at the end of each period) for n periods is ________
questions.explanation: The plain a_n| is the present value of an annuity-immediate, with payments of 1 at the end of each of n periods. Option B (two dots) is the annuity-due, paid at the start of each period, and C (bar) is the continuous annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The international actuarial symbol for the present value of a continuous annuity (payable continuously) for n periods is ________
questions.explanation: The bar over the a, written a-bar_n|, shows that payments are made continuously at a rate of 1 per period. Option A is the annuity-immediate (end-of-period payments) and B, with two dots, is the annuity-due (start-of-period payments).

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The international actuarial symbol for the present value of an annuity-due for n periods is ________
questions.explanation: Two dots over the a, written a-double-dot_n|, mark an annuity-due, where each payment of 1 is made at the start of the period. Option A is the annuity-immediate, paid at the end of each period, and C (bar) is the continuously payable annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity payable at the start of each period is known as?
questions.explanation: An annuity-due makes each payment at the beginning of the period, like rent paid in advance. Options A and B are two names for the same thing, an annuity whose payments come at the end of each period.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A series of payments which does not begin immediately, or in the first period, but only after a period of postponement is called?
questions.explanation: A deferred annuity is one whose first payment is postponed for some periods, so payments start only after the deferment period. Option B starts paying from the first period, and option D (annuity-due) pays at the start of each period from the outset.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: What is an ordinary annuity?

options.a: A series of regular cash flows occurring at the beginning of each period
options.b: A series of regular cash flows occurring at the end of each period
options.d: A series of irregular cash flows

questions.explanation: An ordinary annuity, also called an annuity-immediate or annuity in arrears, pays equal amounts at the end of each period. Option A describes an annuity-due, where each payment is made at the start of the period.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: What is the formula for calculating the future value of an ordinary annuity of P per period for n periods at rate i?
questions.explanation: The accumulated value of an ordinary annuity is P[(1 + i)^n - 1]/i, which is P times s_n|. Option A is the present value formula, P times a_n|, which gives the value today rather than at the end.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Obtain the value of a_5| at 4% (to 4 decimal places).
questions.explanation: a_5| = (1 - v^5)/i = (1 - 1.04^-5)/0.04 = 4.4518, the present value of 1 paid at the end of each year for five years. A five-payment annuity must be worth a bit less than 5, so option C is far too low, and option A is a single discount factor at 5%.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity payable for an unlimited term is called?
questions.explanation: A perpetuity has no end date, so its payments go on forever; a perpetuity of 1 paid at the end of each period has present value 1/i. Option B is an insurance contract that pays at the end of a fixed term or on earlier death, so it is limited in time.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: In actuarial and financial mathematics, an annuity is best described as

options.a: a payment made only when an insured event such as death occurs
options.b: a series of payments made at regular intervals of time
options.c: an irregular stream of cash flows of varying size and timing
options.d: a single lump sum paid at the end of a fixed term

questions.explanation: An annuity is a series of payments made at regular intervals, for a fixed number of years or over a lifetime. Option D is a single payment, not a series. Option A describes an insurance (assurance) benefit, and option C misses the regular intervals that define an annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT another name for an annuity whose payments are made at the END of each period?
questions.explanation: An annuity-due pays at the BEGINNING of each period, so it is not a name for end-of-period payments. Annuity-immediate, ordinary annuity and annuity in arrears (options D, C and A) all mean the same thing: payments at the end of each period.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity of n level payments has its first payment at time 0 and its last payment at time n - 1 (time measured in payment periods). This annuity is called
questions.explanation: Payments at the beginning of each period, from time 0 to time n - 1, make an annuity-due. An annuity-immediate (option A) would pay at times 1 to n. A deferred annuity (option C) starts later than the first period, and a perpetuity (option D) never ends.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity whose first payment is postponed so that the n payments fall at times m + 1, m + 2, ..., m + n is called

options.a: an increasing annuity, with present value written (Ia)_n|
options.b: a perpetuity, with present value written a_inf|
options.c: a deferred annuity, with present value written m|a_n|
options.d: an annuity-due, with present value written a-double-dot_n|

questions.explanation: When the first payment starts some time in the future, the annuity is deferred; with payments at m + 1 to m + n its present value is m|a_n| = v^m a_n|. Option D pays from time 0, option B has no end date, and option A is about payments that grow, not about postponement.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A perpetuity is

options.a: an annuity whose first payment is postponed for several periods
options.b: an annuity whose payments continue only while a named person is alive
options.c: an annuity whose payments increase by a fixed amount each period
options.d: an annuity whose payments continue for ever, with no termination date

questions.explanation: A perpetuity has no termination date: the number of payments n tends to infinity. Option B describes a life annuity, option A a deferred annuity, and option C an increasing (varying) annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A Lagos company has preference shares that pay a fixed dividend of N5 per share at the end of every year with no redemption date. For valuation, this dividend stream is best treated as
questions.explanation: Fixed dividends on a preference (preferred) share with no end date are the classic example of a stream that resembles a perpetuity. A temporary annuity or an n-year annuity-due (options C and B) would stop after a fixed term, and a life annuity (option D) depends on someone staying alive.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: What is the key difference between an annuity-certain and a life (contingent) annuity?

options.a: An annuity-certain uses compound interest; a life annuity uses simple interest
options.b: An annuity-certain pays for a fixed term whatever happens; a life annuity pays only while a named life survives
options.c: An annuity-certain has no end date; a life annuity always has a fixed end date
options.d: An annuity-certain pays at the start of each year; a life annuity pays at the end of each year

questions.explanation: An annuity-certain pays for a fixed term of n years no matter what, while a life (contingent) annuity's payments depend on the survival of a person, written (x). Option D confuses this with arrears versus advance timing, which applies to both kinds. Options C and A are not true distinctions.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A retired civil servant in Ibadan buys a contract that pays her N150,000 at the end of every month for as long as she lives, and payments stop at her death. This is
questions.explanation: Payments that run for the rest of her lifetime and stop at death form a whole-life annuity, which is contingent on survival. Option C is wrong because an annuity-certain pays for a fixed term regardless of death. A perpetuity (option A) never stops, and nothing here is postponed or fixed-term as option B suggests.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity payable to a life aged x that continues during the joint duration of the life of (x) and a term of n years certain (that is, payments stop at death or after n years, whichever comes first) is called

options.b: a temporary life annuity for n years

questions.explanation: Payments that last for n years at most and stop earlier if (x) dies form a temporary life annuity. A whole-life annuity (option D) has no n-year limit, and an annuity-certain (option C) ignores death. A reversionary annuity (option A) starts on the death of another life.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: In International Actuarial Notation, the diaeresis (two dots) placed over the letter a or s, as in the annuity-due symbol a-double-dot_n|, indicates

options.a: that payments are made continuously throughout the period
options.b: acceleration of payments, i.e. payments made at the beginning of each period
options.c: that the payments increase by 1 each period
options.d: that the annuity depends on the survival of a life

questions.explanation: The two dots (trema) symbolise acceleration of payments: each payment is brought forward to the start of the period, giving the annuity-due. Option A is shown by a bar over the symbol, option D by an age suffix such as x, and option C by the prefix I in (Ia).

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: In actuarial notation, a_n| and s_n| (interest effective per period, payments of 1 at the end of each period) stand for

options.a: the present value and the accumulated value (amount) of the annuity respectively
options.b: the present value of an annuity and the present value of an assurance respectively
options.c: the annual payment and the number of payments respectively
options.d: the accumulated value and the present value of the annuity respectively

questions.explanation: The letter a stands for the present value of an annuity, valued at the start, and s stands for its amount, the accumulated value at the end of the term. Option D reverses the two. Option B confuses s with A, the symbol for an assurance, and option C mixes the symbols up with the inputs of the formula.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: With v = 1/(1 + i), the expression (1 - v^n)/i gives

options.a: the present value of an n-period annuity-immediate of 1 per period
options.b: the accumulated value of an n-period annuity-immediate of 1 per period
options.c: the present value of an n-period annuity-due of 1 per period
options.d: the present value of a perpetuity of 1 per period

questions.explanation: (1 - v^n)/i = v + v^2 + ... + v^n, the sum of the present values of payments of 1 at times 1 to n, which is a_n|. Option B is ((1 + i)^n - 1)/i. Option C would use d instead of i in the denominator, and option D is 1/i.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: With d = i/(1 + i), the expression ((1 + i)^n - 1)/d gives

options.a: the accumulated value at time n of an n-period annuity-due of 1 per period
options.b: the present value at time 0 of an n-period deferred annuity
options.c: the accumulated value at time n of an n-period annuity-immediate of 1 per period
options.d: the present value at time 0 of an n-period annuity-due of 1 per period

questions.explanation: Dividing ((1 + i)^n - 1) by d instead of by i gives s-double-dot_n|, the accumulated value of an annuity-due, which is (1 + i) times s_n|. Option C is the same numerator over i. Option D is (1 - v^n)/d, a present value, and option B is v^m a_n|.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Which of the following relationships between annuity functions (rate i per period, v = 1/(1 + i)) is NOT correct?
questions.explanation: Each annuity-due payment is made one period earlier than the matching annuity-immediate payment, so it earns one extra period of interest: s-double-dot_n| = (1 + i) s_n|, not s_n| divided by (1 + i). Options C, B and A are all correct relationships.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An n-payment annuity-due can be split into a payment of 1 at time 0 plus an annuity-immediate of n - 1 payments. Which identity follows from this?
questions.explanation: Payment at time 0 is worth 1, and the remaining n - 1 payments at times 1 to n - 1 are worth a_(n-1)|, so a-double-dot_n| = 1 + a_(n-1)|. Option A counts n + 1 payments. Option B borrows the accumulated-value identity s-double-dot_n| = s_(n+1)| - 1, which does not carry over to present values, and option D subtracts the time-0 payment instead of adding it.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Viewing an (n + 1)-payment annuity-immediate as an n-payment annuity-due starting at time 1 plus a final payment of 1 at time n + 1 gives which accumulated-value identity?
questions.explanation: Valued at time n + 1, the first n payments accumulate to s-double-dot_n| and the last payment adds exactly 1, so s_(n+1)| = s-double-dot_n| + 1. Option C has the wrong sign. Option B forgets the extra interest on the earlier payments, and option A is the formula for s-double-dot_n|, not for s_(n+1)|.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: For a deferred annuity of 1 per period with payments at times m + 1, ..., m + n (interest i per period), which expression is NOT equal to its present value m|a_n|?
questions.explanation: The deferred annuity is an (m + n)-payment annuity with the first m payments removed, so m|a_n| = a_(m+n)| - a_m| = v^m a_n| = (v^m - v^(m+n))/i. Adding a_m| instead of subtracting it counts the missing payments twice. Options D, C and A are all valid forms.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Which identity correctly splits an (m + n)-period annuity-immediate (interest i per period) into two parts?
questions.explanation: The first m payments are worth a_m|, and the last n payments form an annuity starting at time m, worth a_n| at time m and v^m a_n| at time 0. Option C forgets to discount the second block. Option D accumulates instead of discounting, and option A discounts the wrong block.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Why is the present value of a perpetuity-immediate of 1 per period equal to 1/i (for i > 0)?

options.a: Because the last payment is ignored when there are many payments
options.b: Because (1 + i)^n tends to 1 as n tends to infinity
options.c: Because v < 1, so v^n tends to 0 as n tends to infinity in a_n| = (1 - v^n)/i
options.d: Because the payments become smaller each period

questions.explanation: Since v = 1/(1 + i) is less than 1, v^n shrinks to 0 as n grows, so a_n| = (1 - v^n)/i approaches 1/i. Option B is false since (1 + i)^n grows without limit. The payments stay level (option D), and a perpetuity has no last payment (option A).

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The present value of a perpetuity-due of 1 per period (first payment immediately, interest i per period, d = i/(1 + i)) is
questions.explanation: Letting n tend to infinity in a-double-dot_n| = (1 - v^n)/d gives a-double-dot_inf| = 1/d. Option B, 1/i, is the perpetuity-immediate. Option C is just v, and option D equals 1 + i, which is not a present value of an infinite stream.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: For the same positive rate of interest and the same number of level payments, which statement is correct?

options.a: a_n| and a-double-dot_n| (annuity-due) are always equal, because they have the same number of payments
options.b: a-double-dot_n| (annuity-due) is greater than a_n|, because each payment is received one period earlier
options.c: a-double-dot_n| (annuity-due) is smaller than a_n|, because d is smaller than i
options.d: a_n| is greater than a-double-dot_n| (annuity-due), because each payment earns one more period of interest

questions.explanation: Each annuity-due payment comes one period sooner, so it is discounted less and a-double-dot_n| = (1 + i) a_n| is larger. Option D reverses the logic, option A ignores timing, and option C draws the wrong conclusion: dividing by the smaller d makes the annuity-due value larger, not smaller.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A tenant in Yaba pays rent of N400,000 at the beginning of each year for 3 years, starting today. Viewed from the landlord's side today, this stream is
questions.explanation: Rent paid at the start of each period, beginning today, is a standard annuity-due, valued with a-double-dot_3|. An annuity-immediate (option B) would start at the end of the first year. Nothing is postponed, so option D is wrong, and the stream ends after 3 years, unlike option A.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Let i^(m) be the nominal annual rate convertible m times a year equivalent to an effective annual rate i. The present value of an n-year annuity paying 1/m at the end of every 1/m of a year (a total of 1 per year) is
questions.explanation: Paying m times a year in arrears gives a^(m)_n| = (1 - v^n)/i^(m) = (i/i^(m)) a_n|. Option D is the annual-payment a_n|. Option A wrongly raises v to mn even though v is the annual discount factor, and option B, with d^(m), is the m-thly annuity-due.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: With delta = ln(1 + i) the force of interest, the expression (1 - v^n)/delta gives the present value of

options.a: an n-year annuity-due of 1 per year
options.b: an n-year annuity-immediate of 1 per year
options.c: an n-year annuity paid monthly in advance, 1 per year
options.d: an n-year annuity paid continuously at the rate of 1 per year

questions.explanation: Letting the payment frequency m tend to infinity makes i^(m) approach delta, giving the continuous annuity a-bar_n| = (1 - v^n)/delta = (i/delta) a_n|. Options A and B use d and i in the denominator respectively. Option C would use d^(12).

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An n-year increasing annuity-immediate (Ia)_n| (interest i per year, v = 1/(1 + i)) pays

options.a: n at time 1, n - 1 at time 2, ..., 1 at time n, with value (n - a_n|)/i
options.b: 1 at time 0, 2 at time 1, ..., n at time n - 1, with value (n - a_n|)/i
options.c: 1 at each of times 1, 2, ..., n, with value (1 - v^n)/i
options.d: 1 at time 1, 2 at time 2, ..., n at time n, with value (a-double-dot_n| - n v^n)/i

questions.explanation: The increasing annuity-immediate pays 1, 2, ..., n at the end of years 1 to n, and its present value is (Ia)_n| = (a-double-dot_n| - n v^n)/i. Option A is the decreasing annuity (Da)_n|. Option B describes the increasing annuity-due timing but attaches the (Da) formula, and option C is a level annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At the same nominal rate r per year, how does the value of a_3| under SIMPLE interest compare with a_3| under COMPOUND interest (payments of 1 at the end of each year)?

options.a: The two present values are always equal for any n
options.b: The simple-interest present value is lower, because simple interest discounts later payments more
options.c: The comparison depends only on whether payments are in advance or in arrears
options.d: The simple-interest present value is higher, because simple interest discounts later payments less

questions.explanation: At the same nominal rate, compound interest grows faster than simple interest after the first year, so compound discounting makes later payments smaller and the compound a_3| is lower. For example, at 5% the simple-interest value is 2.731 against 2.723 under compound interest. Options B and A are wrong for n > 1, and the timing in option C is not the cause.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate a_8| at an effective rate of interest of 6% per annum (payments of 1 at the end of each year). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: a_8| = (1 - (1.06)^-8)/0.06 = 6.2098. Option B is the annuity-due value, (1.06) x a_8|, which treats the payments as made in advance. Option D is s_8|, the accumulated value, and option A uses only 7 payments.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate s_6| at an effective rate of interest of 7% per annum (payments of 1 at the end of each year, value at time 6). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: s_6| = ((1.07)^6 - 1)/0.07 = 7.1533. Option A is a_6|, the present value rather than the accumulated value. Option C is s-double-dot_6|, the annuity-due amount, and option B uses simple interest on the average payment.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate the annuity-due factor a-double-dot_10| (payments of 1 at the beginning of each year for 10 years) at an effective rate of 5% per annum. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: a-double-dot_10| = (1 - v^10)/d = (1.05) a_10| = 1.05 x 7.7217 = 8.1078. Option B is a_10|, the annuity-immediate. Option A uses 1 + a_10| instead of 1 + a_9|, counting 11 payments. Option C discounts one extra period instead of one fewer.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate s-double-dot_5| (the accumulated value at time 5 of an annuity-due of 1 per year for 5 years) at an effective rate of 8% per annum. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: s-double-dot_5| = ((1.08)^5 - 1)/d with d = 0.08/1.08, which equals (1.08) s_5| = 1.08 x 5.8666 = 6.3359. Option A is s_5|, which treats the payments as made in arrears. Option B is s_6|, which equals s-double-dot_5| + 1, and option D is the present value a-double-dot_5|.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A pension fund will pay N50,000 at the end of each year for 6 years. Using an effective interest rate of 10% per annum, find the present value of these payments to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: PV = 50,000 a_6| = 50,000 x (1 - (1.1)^-6)/0.1 = 50,000 x 4.35526 = N217,763. Option C values the payments in advance (annuity-due). Option D discounts all six payments as if they were paid at time 6, and option B is the accumulated value.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A worker saves N20,000 at the end of each year for 8 years in an account paying 9% effective per annum. What is the accumulated value immediately after the 8th deposit, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: AV = 20,000 s_8| = 20,000 x ((1.09)^8 - 1)/0.09 = 20,000 x 11.02847 = N220,569. Option D treats the deposits as made at the start of each year (s-double-dot_8|). Option B uses simple interest on the average deposit, and option A counts only 7 deposits.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A shop in Surulere is let for 5 years at a rent of N300,000 payable at the beginning of each year. At an effective rate of 12% per annum, find the present value of the rent at the start of the lease, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Rent in advance is an annuity-due: PV = 300,000 a-double-dot_5| = 300,000 x 1.12 x a_5| = 300,000 x 4.03735 = N1,211,205. Option A values the rent in arrears (a_5|). Option D ignores interest altogether, and option C values only the last four payments and forgets the one paid today.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A student deposits N10,000 at the beginning of each year for 6 years into an account earning 8% effective per annum. What is the balance at the end of the 6th year (one year after the last deposit), to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Deposits in advance accumulate as an annuity-due: AV = 10,000 s-double-dot_6| = 10,000 x 1.08 x s_6| = 10,000 x 7.9228 = N79,228. Option A is s_6|, which assumes end-of-year deposits. Option D is the present value, and option B is s_7|, which equals s-double-dot_6| + 1 and so wrongly adds one more deposit.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A loan of N1,000,000 is to be repaid by 5 equal annual instalments, the first one year after the loan is taken. Interest is 15% effective per annum. Find the annual instalment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Instalments in arrears: P = 1,000,000/a_5| = 1,000,000/3.35216 = N298,316. Option C divides by a-double-dot_5|, which treats the first instalment as due immediately. Option B adds one year of simple interest to one-fifth of the loan, and option D divides by s_5|, which gives a sinking-fund deposit, not a loan repayment.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A trader borrows N600,000 at a nominal rate of 24% per annum convertible monthly. She repays it with 12 equal monthly instalments, the first one month after the loan. Find the monthly instalment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The monthly rate is 24%/12 = 2%, so P = 600,000/a_12| at 2% = 600,000/10.5753 = N56,736. Option B wrongly uses 24% as the monthly rate. Option A adds a year of simple interest and divides by 12, and option D treats the instalments as paid in advance.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A company wants N2,000,000 in a fund in 5 years' time to replace a generator. It will make equal deposits at the end of each year into a fund earning 10% effective per annum. Find the annual deposit to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Target = P s_5|, so P = 2,000,000/s_5| = 2,000,000/6.1051 = N327,595. Option B divides by a_5|, which gives the instalment that repays a loan of N2,000,000 today. Option A assumes deposits at the start of each year, and option C ignores interest.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Parents want N500,000 available at the end of 4 years for school fees. They will deposit a level amount at the BEGINNING of each year for 4 years in an account earning 9% effective per annum. Find the annual deposit to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Deposits in advance accumulate as an annuity-due: s-double-dot_4| = 1.09 x s_4| = 1.09 x 4.57313 = 4.98471, so P = 500,000/4.98471 = N100,307. Option C uses s_4|, which treats the deposits as made at year-end. Option A uses a present-value factor, and option B spreads the target equally and discounts it for one year only.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate the deferred annuity factor 3|a_5| at an effective rate of 6% per annum (payments of 1 at times 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: 3|a_5| = v^3 a_5| = (1.06)^-3 x 4.2124 = 3.5368, which also equals a_8| - a_3|. Option C discounts for 4 years, as if the first payment were at time 5 rather than one year after the deferment. Option A ignores the deferment, and option D adds a_3| instead of subtracting it.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A father arranges for his daughter to receive N100,000 at the end of each year for 4 years, with the first payment at the end of year 6. At 10% effective per annum, find the present value today to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The first payment is at time 6, so this is 5|a_4|: PV = 100,000 x (1.1)^-5 x a_4| = 100,000 x 0.62092 x 3.16987 = N196,824. Option D defers 6 years, treating time 6 as the start of the deferred period. Option C ignores the deferment, and option A defers only 4 years, which would put the first payment at time 5.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 6% effective per annum, a_10| = 7.3601 and a_4| = 3.4651. Using these values, find 4|a_6| (an annuity of 1 per year for 6 years, first payment at time 5). Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Removing the first 4 payments from a 10-year annuity leaves payments at times 5 to 10, so 4|a_6| = a_10| - a_4| = 7.3601 - 3.4651 = 3.8950. Option C adds instead of subtracts. Option B is a_6| with no deferment, and option A discounts the difference a second time, even though a_10| - a_4| is already a value at time 0.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An endowment fund will pay a prize of N80,000 at the end of every year for ever. At an effective rate of 8% per annum, how much must be invested today, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: A perpetuity-immediate is worth payment/i = 80,000/0.08 = N1,000,000. Option C is 80,000/d, which is the value if the first prize were paid today. Option B is just one payment with a year's interest, and option A discounts the perpetuity one extra year.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A UNILAG alumni association wants to fund a scholarship of N250,000 per year for ever, with the first award paid today. At an effective rate of 10% per annum, how much must the fund hold today, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Payments starting now form a perpetuity-due: PV = 250,000/d with d = 0.1/1.1, giving 250,000 x 11 = N2,750,000. Option B is the perpetuity-immediate value 250,000/0.1, which misses today's award. Option A discounts a further year, and option C counts today's award twice.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A trust invests N5,000,000 today to pay N400,000 at the end of every year for ever. What effective annual rate of interest is the trust assuming?
questions.explanation: For a perpetuity-immediate, PV = P/i, so i = 400,000/5,000,000 = 8%. Option A is 0.08/1.08, which confuses the interest rate i with the discount rate d. Option B inverts the ratio as 5,000,000/400,000 = 12.5, and option C divides by 4,800,000, which assumes the first payment is made today.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A perpetuity pays N60,000 at the end of each year, but the first payment is made at the end of year 4. At 10% effective per annum, find its present value today to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The perpetuity is worth 60,000/0.1 = 600,000 at time 3 (one year before the first payment), so PV = 600,000 x (1.1)^-3 = N450,789. Option C discounts 4 years, treating 600,000 as a value at time 4. Option A ignores the deferment, and option D uses 1/d, which treats the perpetuity as starting at time 3 instead of time 4.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The rate of discount is d = 0.05 per annum, so that the present value of a perpetuity-due of 1 per year is 1/d = 20. What is the present value of a perpetuity-immediate of 1 per year at the same rate?
questions.explanation: The perpetuity-due is the perpetuity-immediate plus a payment of 1 now, so a_inf| = a-double-dot_inf| - 1 = 20 - 1 = 19. Check: i = d/(1 - d) = 0.05/0.95 and 1/i = 19. Option D adds the extra payment instead of removing it, option C ignores timing, and option B uses i = 0.05 (which is d) and then divides by 1.05.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 7% effective per annum, a_9| = 6.5152. Using this value, find a-double-dot_10| (an annuity-due of 1 per year for 10 years) to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: An annuity-due of 10 payments is a payment of 1 now plus an annuity-immediate of 9 payments: a-double-dot_10| = 1 + a_9| = 1 + 6.5152 = 7.5152. Option B gives a-double-dot_9|, which has the wrong number of payments. Option C wrongly converts a_9| to a due basis before adding 1, and option D adds 1.07 instead of 1.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 5% effective per annum, s-double-dot_7| (annuity-due) = 8.5491. Find s_8| to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Using s_(n+1)| = s-double-dot_n| + 1, s_8| = 8.5491 + 1 = 9.5491. Option A subtracts 1. Option D accumulates s-double-dot_7| one more year, which misses the final payment of 1 at time 8. Option C is s_7|.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 4% effective per annum, a_12| = 9.3851. Find s_12| to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: s_12| = (1 + i)^12 a_12| = (1.04)^12 x 9.3851 = 15.0258. Option B accumulates for only one year, which gives a-double-dot_12|. Option C discounts instead of accumulating, and option D uses simple interest for 12 years.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 4% effective per annum, a_n| = 10.5631 for some whole number n. Find v^n to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: From a_n| = (1 - v^n)/i, v^n = 1 - i a_n| = 1 - 0.04 x 10.5631 = 0.5775. Option D is i a_n| itself, which equals 1 - v^n. Option C wrongly inverts, and option A uses d = 0.04/1.04 in place of i.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A principal of N400,000 is used to pay N50,000 at the end of each year for as long as possible at 5% effective per annum. How many full payments of N50,000 can be made? (a_10| = 7.7217 and a_11| = 8.3064 at 5%.)
questions.explanation: The equation of value 50,000 a_n| = 400,000 gives a_n| = 8, which lies between a_10| = 7.7217 and a_11| = 8.3064, so only 10 full payments are possible (a smaller final payment settles the rest). Option D needs a_11| = 8.3064, which is more than the N400,000 available. Option B ignores interest (400,000/50,000), and option A is one payment too few.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A principal of N400,000 pays N50,000 at the end of each year for 10 years at 5% effective per annum. To exhaust the fund exactly, what EXTRA amount must be paid together with the 10th payment at the end of year 10? Give the answer to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Extra amount = 400,000(1.05)^10 - 50,000 s_10| = 651,558 - 628,895 = N22,663. Option C is that amount carried one more year, which is the smaller final payment if it were paid alone at the end of year 11. Option D is the shortfall measured at time 0 (400,000 - 50,000 a_10|), not carried forward to time 10, and option B is the whole final payment (the regular N50,000 plus the extra), not the extra amount alone.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A 10-year annuity-immediate of N1 per year has a present value of 7.0236. At which effective annual rate of interest was it valued?
questions.explanation: At 7%, a_10| = (1 - (1.07)^-10)/0.07 = 7.0236, which matches. At 6% (option C) a_10| = 7.3601, at 8% (option A) it is 6.7101 and at 9% (option B) it is 6.4177. A higher rate always gives a lower present value.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A contract pays N25,000 at the end of every quarter for 3 years. Interest is 12% per annum convertible quarterly. Find the present value at the start, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The quarterly rate is 12%/4 = 3% and there are 12 payments, so PV = 25,000 a_12| at 3% = 25,000 x 9.95400 = N248,850. Option B values annual payments of N100,000 at 12% effective, which is a different rate basis. Option C treats the payments as made in advance, and option D uses 12% as the quarterly rate.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A civil servant saves N5,000 at the end of each month for 2 years in a cooperative account paying 18% per annum convertible monthly. Find the accumulated value after the last deposit, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The monthly rate is 1.5% and there are 24 deposits: AV = 5,000 s_24| at 1.5% = 5,000 x 28.6335 = N143,168. Option A uses 18% as the monthly rate, option B applies simple interest of 18% to all deposits, and option D treats the deposits as made at the start of each month.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity pays N100,000 at the end of every half-year for 3 years. Interest is 12% per annum convertible quarterly. Find the present value to the nearest naira. (First find the effective rate per half-year.)
questions.explanation: Payments are half-yearly but interest is converted quarterly, so the effective half-yearly rate is (1.03)^2 - 1 = 6.09%, and PV = 100,000 a_6| at 6.09% = N490,345. Option B uses 6%, which is the nominal half-yearly rate, not the effective one. Option D uses the 3% quarterly rate with half-yearly payments, and option A counts 12 payments.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A tenant pays N20,000 at the end of every quarter for 2 years. Interest is 10% per annum convertible half-yearly. Find the present value of the payments to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: The effective quarterly rate is (1.05)^0.5 - 1 = 2.4695%, so PV = 20,000 a_8| at that rate = N143,589. Option C uses 2.5%, which simply halves the half-yearly rate. Option D uses the half-yearly rate of 5% per quarter, and option B treats the stream as 4 half-yearly payments of N20,000 and doubles the result.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity of N120,000 per year is payable in monthly instalments of N10,000 at the end of each month for 5 years. Interest is 10% effective per annum. Using a^(12)_5| = (1 - v^5)/i^(12), where i^(12) is the equivalent nominal rate convertible monthly, find the present value to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Here i^(12) = 12[(1.1)^(1/12) - 1] = 0.095690, so a^(12)_5| = (1 - (1.1)^-5)/0.095690 = 3.96154 and PV = 120,000 x 3.96154 = N475,385. Option C treats the payments as annual in arrears (120,000 a_5|). Option B treats 10% as a nominal rate convertible monthly, and option A uses d^(12), which gives the monthly annuity-due.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity of N240,000 per year is paid in quarterly instalments of N60,000 at the BEGINNING of each quarter for 3 years. Interest is 8% effective per annum. Using a-double-dot^(4)_3| = (1 - v^3)/d^(4) (annuity-due payable quarterly), find the present value to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Here d^(4) = 4[1 - (1.08)^(-1/4)] = 0.076225, so PV = 240,000 x (1 - (1.08)^-3)/0.076225 = N649,131. Option B uses i^(4), which gives quarterly payments in arrears. Option A treats the payments as annual in advance, and option D as annual in arrears.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate a-bar_10|, the present value of an annuity paid continuously at the rate of 1 per year for 10 years, at an effective rate of 6% per annum. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: a-bar_10| = (1 - v^10)/delta with delta = ln(1.06) = 0.058269, giving 0.441605/0.058269 = 7.5787. Option D is a_10| (end-year payments) and option C is a-double-dot_10| (start-year payments); the continuous value lies between the two. Option A multiplies by delta instead of dividing.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A company in Port Harcourt promises an employee N500,000 at the end of each year for 10 years starting one year after her retirement. It funds this with 8 equal payments made at the BEGINNING of each year over the 8 years before retirement. At 8% effective per annum, find the annual funding payment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: PV at retirement = 500,000 a_10| = 500,000 x 6.71008 = 3,355,041. This must equal P s-double-dot_8| = P x 11.48756, so P = N292,059. Option A uses s_8|, which treats the payments as made in arrears. Option C wrongly divides by a present-value factor, and option B ignores discounting of the pension.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An investment pays N10,000 at the end of year 1, N20,000 at the end of year 2, and so on up to N50,000 at the end of year 5. At 10% effective per annum, find the present value to the nearest naira, using (Ia)_5| = (a-double-dot_5| - 5v^5)/i.
questions.explanation: (Ia)_5| = (4.1699 - 5 x 0.62092)/0.1 = 10.6526, so PV = 10,000 x 10.6526 = N106,526. Option C uses a_5| instead of a-double-dot_5| in the formula. Option A values the payments in advance, and option D is the decreasing annuity (Da)_5|, which pays 50,000 first.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A machine's maintenance savings are N50,000 at the end of year 1, N40,000 at the end of year 2, and so on down to N10,000 at the end of year 5. At 10% effective per annum, find the present value to the nearest naira, using (Da)_5| = (5 - a_5|)/i.
questions.explanation: (Da)_5| = (5 - 3.7908)/0.1 = 12.0921, so PV = 10,000 x 12.0921 = N120,921. Option B is the increasing annuity (Ia)_5|, which reverses the order. Option D uses a-double-dot_5| in the formula, and option A values the average payment of N30,000 as a level annuity.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A business receives N100,000 at the end of year 1, and each later payment is N20,000 more than the previous one, for 6 payments in all. At 8% effective per annum, find the present value using P a_n| + D (a_n| - n v^n)/i, to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: PV = 100,000 a_6| + 20,000 (a_6| - 6v^6)/0.08 = 462,288 + 20,000 x 10.5233 = N672,753. Option D uses a-double-dot_6| instead of a_6| inside the increasing part, which overstates it. Option B uses 5v^6 instead of 6v^6, and option A values the average payment of N150,000 as level.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A franchise pays N100,000 at the end of year 1, and each later payment is 5% higher than the one before, for 10 payments. At 10% effective per annum, find the present value to the nearest naira, using (1 - ((1 + k)/(1 + i))^n)/(i - k).
questions.explanation: With k = 0.05 and i = 0.10, PV = 100,000 x (1 - (1.05/1.10)^10)/0.05 = 100,000 x 7.43981 = N743,981. Option C uses i + k in the denominator instead of i - k. Option B ignores the 5% growth, and option D values the stream as if paid in advance.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Under SIMPLE interest at 6% per annum, the present value of 1 due at time t is 1/(1 + 0.06t). Find a_4| (payments of 1 at the end of each year for 4 years) under simple interest, to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: a_4| = 1/1.06 + 1/1.12 + 1/1.18 + 1/1.24 = 0.9434 + 0.8929 + 0.8475 + 0.8065 = 3.4902. Option C is the compound-interest value (1 - (1.06)^-4)/0.06 = 3.4651, which is slightly lower. Option A uses simple discount (1 - 0.06t) instead, and option D discounts all four payments from time 4.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A 7-year annuity-immediate pays N1 at the end of each year (5% effective per annum). What is the value of the whole annuity at time 3, just after the 3rd payment? Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: At time 3, the 3 payments already made are worth s_3| = 3.1525 and the 4 still to come are worth a_4| = 3.5460, so the value is 6.6985, which is also (1.05)^3 a_7|. Option B is the value at time 0 and option C is the value at time 7. Option D discounts the future payments by one extra year.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A loan of N1,000,000 is repaid by 5 equal annual instalments in arrears at 15% effective per annum. Just after the 2nd instalment is paid, what is the present value of the remaining instalments (the outstanding loan), to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: The instalment is P = 1,000,000/a_5| = 298,316, and 3 instalments remain, so the outstanding loan = P a_3| = 298,315.55 x 2.283225 = N681,122. Option B subtracts the instalments without allowing for interest. Option D values only 2 remaining instalments, and option A assumes 2/5 of the loan has been repaid.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A loan of N1,000,000 is repaid by 5 equal annual instalments in arrears at 15% effective per annum (instalment = 1,000,000/a_5|). What is the total interest paid over the life of the loan, to the nearest naira?
questions.explanation: Total paid = 5 x 298,316 = 1,491,578, so the total interest is 1,491,578 - 1,000,000 = N491,578. Option D is the total paid, not the interest. Option C charges 15% simple interest on the full loan every year, and option B uses annuity-due instalments.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An annuity pays N100,000 per year for 5 years at 10% effective per annum. By how much does the present value of the annuity-due exceed the present value of the annuity-immediate? Give the answer to the nearest naira. (Hint: a-double-dot_n| - a_n| = 1 - v^n.)
questions.explanation: a-double-dot_5| - a_5| = 1 - v^5 = 1 - 0.62092 = 0.37908, so the difference is N37,908 (the payment at time 0 gained minus the payment at time 5 lost, in PV terms). Option A is 1.1 x i x a_5|, which mixes two formulas. Option B is only v^5, and option D adds simple interest of N10,000 a year.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The annual effective rate of discount is d = 8%, so v = 0.92. Calculate a-double-dot_4| = (1 - v^4)/d (annuity-due of 1 per year for 4 years) to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: a-double-dot_4| = (1 - (0.92)^4)/0.08 = (1 - 0.716393)/0.08 = 3.5451. Option D divides by i = d/(1 - d) = 0.086957, which gives a_4|. Option C wrongly treats 8% as the interest rate i, and option B accumulates the answer by one extra year.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: The discount factor is v = 0.9 per year. Calculate a_5| (payments of 1 at the end of each year for 5 years) to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: v = 0.9 means 1 + i = 1/0.9, so i = 1/9, and a_5| = (1 - 0.59049)/(1/9) = 3.6856, the same as 0.9 + 0.81 + ... + 0.59049. Option D divides by 0.1, which is d, and so gives a-double-dot_5|. Option B is a_4|, one payment too few, and option C discounts all payments from time 5.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 6% effective per annum, s_5| = 5.6371 and s_3| = 3.1836. Using s_(m+n)| = (1 + i)^n s_m| + s_n|, find s_8| to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: The first 5 payments are worth s_5| at time 5 and earn 3 more years of interest, while the last 3 payments add s_3|: s_8| = (1.06)^3 x 5.6371 + 3.1836 = 9.8975. Option B forgets the 3 years of extra interest. Option C accumulates for 5 years instead of 3, and option A also accumulates s_3|, which is already a time-8 value.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 8% effective per annum, a_6| = 4.6229 and a_4| = 3.3121. Using a_(m+n)| = a_n| + v^n a_m|, find a_10| to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: The last 4 payments are worth a_4| at time 6, i.e. v^6 a_4| at time 0, so a_10| = 4.6229 + (1.08)^-6 x 3.3121 = 6.7101. Option C adds the two factors with no discounting. Option B discounts for 4 years instead of 6, and option D accumulates instead of discounting.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An investor pays N2,100,000 for a perpetuity of N100,000 per year with the first payment made immediately. What effective annual rate of interest does this imply?
questions.explanation: For a perpetuity-due, price = payment/d, so d = 100,000/2,100,000 = 1/21, and i = d/(1 - d) = (1/21)/(20/21) = 1/20 = 5%. Option D, 4.76%, is d itself, which treats the stream as a perpetuity-immediate. Option A deducts the immediate payment twice (100,000/1,900,000), and option B computes d/(1 + d) instead of d/(1 - d).

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A landlord grants a 10-year lease on a property in Abuja for N3,000,000 today, to be paid by 10 equal annual instalments with the first instalment due immediately. At 12% effective per annum, find each instalment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Instalments starting now form an annuity-due: P = 3,000,000/a-double-dot_10| = 3,000,000/6.32825 = N474,065. Option B divides by a_10|, which treats the instalments as paid in arrears. Option A ignores interest, and option C divides by an accumulated-value factor.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: Calculate the deferred annuity-due factor 2|a-double-dot_4| (payments of 1 at times 2, 3, 4 and 5) at 9% effective per annum, using m|a-double-dot_n| = v^m a-double-dot_n|. Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: 2|a-double-dot_4| = (1.09)^-2 x a-double-dot_4| = 0.84168 x 3.5313 = 2.9722, which also equals 3|a_4| because the payments fall at times 2 to 5. Option D uses a_4|, which moves every payment one year later. Option A ignores the deferment, and option C discounts for only 1 year.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: At 10% effective per annum, what is the present value of a perpetuity-immediate of N1 per year minus a 10-year annuity-immediate of N1 per year (that is, the value of payments from year 11 onwards)? Give your answer to 4 decimal places.
questions.explanation: Payments from time 11 onwards form 10|a_inf| = v^10/i = 1/i - a_10| = 10 - 6.1446 = 3.8554. Option C subtracts the annuity-due, which removes the wrong payments. Option D starts from the perpetuity-due 1/d, and option A discounts one year too many.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: A loan of N800,000 is repaid by level instalments at the end of each year for 6 years, but the first instalment is made at the end of year 3 (a 2-year grace period). At 7% effective per annum, find the instalment to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Payments at times 3 to 8 form 2|a_6| = v^2 a_6| = 0.873439 x 4.766540 = 4.163280, so P = 800,000/4.163280 = N192,156. Option D ignores the grace period. Option B defers 3 years instead of 2, and option C adds 2 years of interest and then ignores further interest.

questions.topic: Annuities and Annuity Functions
questions.question: An insurance company in Lagos buys an annuity-certain paying N1,000,000 at the beginning of each year for 15 years. At 6% effective per annum, find its purchase price (present value) to the nearest naira.
questions.explanation: Payments in advance give PV = 1,000,000 a-double-dot_15| = 1,000,000 x 1.06 x 9.7122 = N10,294,984. Option B values the payments in arrears. Option A uses 1 + a_15|, which counts 16 payments, and option D counts only 14 payments.
